claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total Boolean language F defined in proof.md Section 1, at actual input length N=|x|. For N=0 the output is 0. For N>=1 let B be the least positive integer with B^5>32*N^3 and let k be the least prime at least B; if k>=N output 0. Put m=N-k, r=ceil(m/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)); if t>=r or k*t<r*(r+1) output 0. Read the first k input bits as the lower coefficients of the monic degree-k polynomial Q(Z)=Z^k+sum_j b_j Z^j over F_2; test Q exactly by checking Z^(2^k)=Z mod Q and gcd(Q,Z^2+Z)=1, and output 0 if the test fails. Otherwise let K=F_2[Z]/(Q), pad the remaining m payload bits with zeros into r blocks of k bits read in the polynomial basis with the first bit as the constant coefficient, set y_i=a_i^(2^(r+2-i)-1) for 1<=i<=r, and output the constant coefficient pi in K of the elementary symmetric polynomial of order t in y_1,...,y_r. One fixed deterministic polynomial-time evaluator computes F at every length; the NP verifier accepts exactly the empty witness on inputs the evaluator accepts, so the witness bound is 0 and the witness is never a circuit input. The first k bits are counted in N; the zero padding is inside the injective F_2-linear payload map and adds no circuit input.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total uniform polynomial-time Boolean family, hence one language in NP with witness bound zero, C_B2(F_N) >= 4*N - 87*N^(4/5) for every integer N >= 1024, where C_B2(F_N) is the minimum number of gates in a full Li-Yang B2 circuit computing the length-N restriction of F. Therefore liminf over all integer N of C_B2(F_N)/N >= 4 in the full Li-Yang B2 model at actual input length N=|x|. Equivalently, for every real epsilon>0 there exists N_epsilon such that every integer N>=N_epsilon satisfies C_B2(F_N) >= (4-epsilon)*N.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: Auxiliary lemma (unscored, string claim): for the potential family V = s + beta*q + alpha*I with alpha,beta >= 0, the largest coefficient theta such that every gate-elimination step satisfies Delta V <= theta*Delta a, with Delta a in {0,-1}, is exactly 4, attained precisely when alpha = beta + 2 with beta >= 4. Hence no reweighting of this potential family yields a coefficient above 4. Full proof: optimality.md.
title: Published coefficient/exponent pair (4, 1) for the fixed BK affine-disperser family
